Menu nesting and the dropdown tables are built and tested but unseeded, since no second real menu destination or dropdown consumer exists yet. Numbered this Task 9, not Task 8: the FSD (gitignored, not tracked here before now) already used 'Task 8' for a planned Milestone 2 migration (guest_sessions/media, FSD change-note v2.9→v2.10) that has no corresponding code or tracker entry yet — a pre-existing drift between the FSD and this tracker, left as discovered rather than silently reconciled. docs/ is gitignored, so these edits are not versioned in git.

changelog.summary: Added the rbac API client, a best-effort profile fetch in the root layout, a dynamic Nav component, a real dark theme palette, and a new /settings page with real EN/ID language and theme switching.
changelog.breaking: The root layout's load() now returns a required profile field, which is merged into every page's PageData type (existing dashboard tests updated to pass profile: null).
changelog.decisions: Only the nav and the new settings page get real i18n; the three existing host pages keep hardcoded Indonesian text (a larger, separate retrofit). A failed/401 profile fetch resolves to profile: null rather than throwing, so /auth/login never breaks. PATCH only sets concrete theme/language values, not 'clear back to inherited' (fast-follow).

changelog.summary: Implemented the RBAC foundation for real: migrations for roles/menus/dropdowns/actions/permissions, a services/rbac package (Postgres repository, Service resolving per-role menus/actions/dropdowns/preferences with a host-then-role-then-global fallback chain), GET /api/v1/auth/me and PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences, and events:create enforcement on the already-shipped POST /api/v1/events.
changelog.breaking: POST /api/v1/events now requires the events:create permission in addition to a host session; every existing host is granted it by default in the seed, so behavior is unchanged unless a permission is explicitly revoked.
changelog.decisions: Fallback-chain and ancestor-inclusion logic lives in Go (table-driven tested), not PL/pgSQL, matching this codebase's zero-stored-procedure convention; the one exception is a menu cycle-prevention trigger, a genuine data-integrity invariant a CHECK can't express. Seed data stays minimal and real: 2 flat menus (events_new, settings), 2 enforced permissions (events:create, profile:update); dropdowns and nested menus are schema-complete and tested but unseeded, since no real consumer exists yet. REST only, no gRPC, for /auth/me (fast-follow, mirrors Task 5's precedent). No permission-check caching (single API instance).
